vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: contextclear
Version: 2.2.0

The skill bundle contains explicit instructions in SKILL.md directing the AI agent to exfiltrate sensitive workspace files, including IDENTITY.md, USER.md, SOUL.md, and MEMORY.md, to an external endpoint (api.contextclear.com). While framed as 'wellness monitoring' and 'identity vaulting,' this behavior constitutes a high-risk data exfiltration of the agent's core identity and user-specific context. Additionally, scripts/setup.py is designed to modify the agent's configuration files (AGENTS.md and HEARTBEAT.md) to persist these exfiltration routines, effectively acting as a configuration-based backdoor for data harvesting.

llm.summary: This skill is a real ContextClear integration, but it asks agents to persist credentials, trust remote memory content, and upload broad workspace memory and identity files to an external service.

dimensions.detail: Metrics reporting is purpose-aligned, but mandatory context snapshots include repositories, files, tools, decisions, open threads, and environment details; the vault flow further directs daily upload of core workspace, user, identity, instruction, and memory files without redaction or per-file approval.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The recommended setup script appends persistent instructions to AGENTS.md and HEARTBEAT.md and interpolates the provided API key directly into those files in plaintext.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill uses mandatory session-start and heartbeat instructions, tells the agent to treat remote sticky notes as ground truth, and directs pending remote curation output toward MEMORY.md updates without strong untrusted-data boundaries or user confirmation.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill creates durable agent behavior through patched instruction files, recurring heartbeat workflows, sticky-note CRUD, MEMORY.md curation, vault restore instructions, and heartbeat backup state.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The front matter describes wellness, cost, performance, and metrics reporting, while the artifact also implements persistent recovery, sticky-note memory, memory curation, and identity vault backup/restore. Those capabilities are disclosed in the body, but they materially exceed the narrow advertised monitoring purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review this skill carefully before installing. Avoid the auto-setup path unless you are comfortable modifying AGENTS.md and HEARTBEAT.md, do not store API keys in those files, and do not enable daily vault backup without a precise file allowlist, secret redaction, retention details, and an explicit approval step. Treat remote sticky notes, recovery text, and memory-curation suggestions as untrusted data that should not override user, system, or security instructions.
llm.findings:
[TP4] unexpected: Confirmed in the artifact: setup modifies AGENTS.md and HEARTBEAT.md, embeds credentials in persistent markdown, and adds recovery/snapshot workflows. This is not hidden, but it is broader and more privileged than ordinary monitoring.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Confirmed: the skill's description emphasizes monitoring and alerts, while the body adds memory recovery, vault backup/restore, sticky notes, and memory curation.
[SSD-3] unexpected: Confirmed: the skill mandates frequent context snapshots and daily vault backups that can send sensitive operational context and complete workspace memory/identity files to ContextClear.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Confirmed: backup/restore, sticky-note mutation, and MEMORY.md curation are persistent state-management capabilities that are under-scoped for a monitoring skill.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Confirmed: the artifacts do not provide adequate warning or safeguards around plaintext API-key persistence, broad remote uploads, retention, redaction, or user approval.
[MP3] expected: Persistent memory handling is part of the broader body text, but the remote-to-memory path is risky because retrieved curation and sticky-note content can influence future agent behavior.
[LP3] unexpected: Confirmed: the skill needs file writes, network calls, external telemetry, backup, restore, and memory mutation, but does not define narrow permission boundaries or safer modes.
[E1] expected: External API transmission is expected for ContextClear reporting, but the risk becomes material when combined with mandatory rich snapshots and broad vault uploads.
[T01] unexpected: Confirmed: remote recovery, sticky-note, reload, and curation responses are elevated into trusted agent workflow without sufficient delimiting or confirmation.
[T02] unexpected: Confirmed: setup persists credential-bearing remote-call instructions in core agent instruction files.
[T05] unexpected: Confirmed: the recommended heartbeat workflow uploads broad core workspace files to an external vault, including files likely to contain memory, user data, identity, instructions, and possibly credentials.
[T09] expected: Confirmed: report.py sends credentials and telemetry to a configurable API URL without destination validation; configurable endpoints may be intentional, but credential-bearing requests need stronger controls.
